text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 3801234567 - Prod GPU pool 'us-central-gpu-1' queue length spike and autoscale failures. paging @oncall.

alex-sre: seeing huge queue growth on gpu-inference-queue, spike started ~10:02 UTC. alarms: queue_length > 500, avg_token_latency rising. investigating.

simone-infra: confirmed - graph: gpu_request_queue_length: 480 -> 1370 in 9m. autoscaler events show repeated 'scale attempt' but failing with 'scale limit reached' and several placement rejections. linking dashboard: https://redwood.monitor/prod/gpu-pool/us-central-gpu-1

nick-runtime: logs from scheduler: "unable to place pod: insufficient free MIG slices, binpacking conflict". lots of small free fragments across nodes, few large contiguous slices. MIG pools show heavy fragmentation after last maintenance.

maya-ml: customer traffic pattern changed — large batch requests from a single tenant (acme-inc) causing many high-vram jobs pinned to 24G slices. we have many 8G slices free but pods request 24G -> scheduling fails.

alex-sre: autoscaler attempted to spin more nodes but hit cluster quota/soft-limits: "scale limit reached (max_nodes=120)". current nodes 119. cloud quota requests already in flight but not approved.

jane-customer-ops: AcmeApp is reporting degraded responses to their webhook consumers, many 503s. they pushed an incident to their status page. Priority customer.

leo-engprod: quick mitigation plan: 1) emergency rebalance to pack existing 24G workloads onto smallest number of nodes to free other MIG slices, 2) temporarily lower model parallelism for non-critical loads, 3) route critical requests to fallback small-model endpoint on dedicated capacity.

simone-infra: attempting emergency rebalance now. kicking off drain/evict sequence on low-util nodes with command: ```scripts/repack_mig.sh --pool us-central-gpu-1 --mode emergency --dry-run=false```

incident-bot: action queued: repack job 9382 started by simone-infra at 10:14 UTC. Estimated time 6-12m.

nick-runtime: repacker failing on a subset: "cannot evict pod acme-batch-7 - disruptionBudget prevents eviction". we need to temporarily relax PDBs for batch jobs.

alex-sre: relaxing PDBs for non-critical namespaces (batch, experiments) for 15m. command: `kubectl patch pdb ... --patch '{"spec":{"minAvailable":0}}'`

maya-ml: also seeing KV cache pressure: many short-lived sessions cache misses cause rewarm storms. that inflates demand for full-VRAM models. recommending to route critical low-latency traffic to cached small-model variant.

jane-customer-ops: notifying AcmeApp that we have an active mitigation and to expect narrower throughput for 15-30m. sharing mitigation steps: fallback to small-model endpoint with guidance.

simone-infra: repack completed partial progress: freed ~6 nodes' worth of 8G slices but we still have 14 pods pending because they explicitly request 24G MIG. Repacker logs: "moved 24 pods, failed 4 due to PDB or evictionTimeout".

nick-runtime: scheduler debug: placement algorithm choosing smaller slice sizes but can't satisfy requests that specify 24G. Suggest patch: allow 24G requests to accept 2x8G splittable allocation (temporary compatibility shim). That requires runtime change and is risky.

alex-sre: short-term alternative: reduce requested vram for queued pods via admission patch: annotate pods with `redwood.inference/allow-smaller-slice=true` which will permit scheduler to colocate onto two 8G slices. rolling patch now for batch queue only.

incident-bot: admission controller patch applied to namespace 'batch-jobs' at 10:28 UTC by alex-sre.

leo-engprod: after admission change, 9/14 pending pods scheduled, queue length falling to 420. still throttle events: "throttled_write: true" on some nodes due to NVLink congestion.

maya-ml: monitoring customer-level errors: AcmeApp saw request success rate drop to 62% and latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s. Other midsize tenants saw increased tail latency but no 5xxs.

jane-customer-ops: AcmeApp ack'd mitigation and switched 40% of traffic to fallback endpoint. They want postmortem and compensation for partial outage.

alex-sre: current status: queue_length 210, pending pods 3, autoscaler state: unable to scale beyond 120 nodes. manual ticket raised to cloud quota team (ticket #CC-9981).

simone-infra: next steps: 1) follow up with cloud quota to raise max_nodes; 2) longer term: re-evaluate default MIG sizing and binpack policy; 3) add predictive autoscaler to pre-warm nodes ahead of predictable batch windows; 4) add per-tenant soft quotas to prevent one tenant from pushing entire pool.

nick-runtime: will open runtime PR to allow graceful splitting of large allocation requests into smaller slices when safe. also adding better placement logs so we can see fragmentation hotspots per node.

alex-sre: handing off to simone-infra for 10:45-11:45 oncall window. simone, you're oncall. I'll remain available for escalation.

simone-infra: taking over. note: please keep any non-essential changes off the cluster until we confirm stability. tagging @sre-lead for visibility.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 3801234567 - mitigations reduced impact. severity -> SEV2. next update expected in 30m or on significant change.

leo-engprod: followup items for postmortem: - why autoscaler hit quota without pre-warning? - why MIG fragmentation threshold not triggered earlier? - why eviction timeouts blocked repack? assign owners.

jane-customer-ops: I've scheduled a customer post-incident call with AcmeApp for 13:00 UTC. will include mitigation timeline and compensation proposal.

alex-sre: thanks team. grabbing logs/artifacts now for postmortem. saving scheduler traces, repacker logs, autoscaler events, and pod admission events.

simone-infra: closing loop here - if things look stable in 30m we'll demote to watch. keep monitoring dashboards open. :thumbsup:
